item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 11 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 session was mostly confused wandering, unhelpful NPCs, an accidentally freed lich, and no clearer idea where Mordus went.

Tipa’s Frosthaven group cheesed Scenario 120’s orb objective while a brutal random-card rule made Trapper planning gloriously fall apart.

Roger explains why World of Warcraft: Forever’s group-dependent, friction-heavy combat and rigid old-school rotations are pretty much the opposite of his MMO tastes.

Frank digs into Towers of Babble’s hardest design problems, contrasting its procedural puzzle chaos with Order of the Sinking Star’s hand-built intent.

Frostilyte finds Annihilated’s branching routes and companion-dependent combat compelling, even if its story differences don’t always justify every replay equally.

Azuriel eyes World of Warcraft: Forever’s huge launch numbers with skepticism, mostly wondering whether horizontal progression can really keep WoW players hooked.

Margot picked the Steam Deck for travel, then got completely absorbed by Minishoot’ Adventures and its charming twin-stick Zelda-like exploration.

David’s Gunderholfen party keeps camping in the dungeon, explores Level 5, and very possibly trusts some suspiciously friendly dwarves way too much.

Wilhelm sizes up EVE Online’s Fractured Skies, from free Omega bait to CCP’s latest attempt at making new players stick around.

Ramen Junkie likes Earthrise Smokescreen’s G1-accurate robot mode and shoulder cannons, but thinks the rally-car alt mode really needed bolder paint.

Tim Bray’s latest link roundup fixates on AI slop-spotting, with Pangram, STORIED · COLORS, and some uneasy anti-LLM soul-searching.

Juhis riffs on prolific blogging as a learning tool, arguing developers should write things down early and search their own notes first.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 10 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 session is all tangled quests, shady Driftwood basements, ghostly nuisances, and very little concern for dead Magisters.

Tipa riffs on EA’s Saudi-led buyout news, then happily dives into Steam’s Wing Commander drop and the cozy blobber Underkeep.

Bhagpuss finds Soulframe’s Alca intriguingly open, but quickly ditches the objective rails to wander and poke at its early systems.

Marc revisits Boom Blox Bash Party, the Steven Spielberg-and-EA Wii oddity that turned motion controls and physics puzzles into a clever family game.

Wilhelm settles into WoW Forever’s vanilla comfort, alt-hopping through Azeroth while Blizzard boasts its biggest WoW launch ever.

Heartless celebrates the Packers’ Foxboro rout, with Jordan Love airing it out despite a shaky run game and Josh Jacobs getting hurt.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from Retroshelf and Ocarina of Time to Godzilla Minus Zero, card magic, church hangouts, and badminton.

Warner vents about Apple’s maddening AirPods, HomePods, Siri, and timer-routing weirdness, where the only consistent thing is inconsistency.

Bruce Schneier flags a nasty decade-old OpenSSH flaw affecting musl-based Linux systems, where oversized passwords can bypass disabled password logins.

Dave Winer argues the web’s old easy interop got captured by big companies, while his Markdown feed unexpectedly pulls more traffic than HTML.

Cristian shares a video on Ubuntu’s rise as a would-be Windows killer and its later loss of desktop momentum.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 9 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 notes hit ghosts, voidwoken, cursed gear, and a few bleak animal encounters around Reaper’s Bluffs.

Magi says Sephiria turns familiar roguelike ideas into something special with cute art, inventive builds, and smart inventory tactics.

Kimimi loves how Haruka 3 toughens up Nozomi, reworks the series formula, and drops the priestess into a fantasy Genji-Heike war.

Krista finds RATATAN’s Patapon-style rhythm roguelike battles catchy and chaotic, even if nailing the timing takes some practice.

Wilhelm tracks Fantasy Critic’s stretch run as Zelda: Ocarina of Time posts a huge 95.6 and rockets Corr into second.

The Chronicler unboxes Twilight Struggle’s 20th Anniversary edition, spotlighting revamped art, stacked extras, and a new Red Sun Rising scenario.

Andrew Plotkin rounds up five visual-first puzzle oddities, with Rivage standing out as pretty and clever but ultimately more procedural than revelatory.

Nicole admires a 1970 Royal 240 ultraportable typewriter, digging into its fake-wood charm, odd icon keys, and possible overseas roots.

Juhis reflects on balancing enthusiasm and anxiety in Djangonaut Space, while leaning on community, mentoring, and note-taking to regroup.

Bruce Schneier sketches AI security in three buckets—security of AI, with AI, and from AI—after a dense, wide-ranging conference.

Dave Winer links John Gruber’s concise Markdown authorship note, then admits JBL Tune Flex earbuds were better once he wore them right.

Cristian posts a quick gag image riffing on OpenAI, Chrome, and RAM-heavy browsing habits.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 8 November 2026
item.description:
Stargrace introduces a WoW druid whose love of nature is complicated by clumsiness, shyness, and a hilariously disastrous acorn allergy.

Bhagpuss dives into Soulframe’s pre-alpha, curious whether Digital Extremes’ fantasy spin on Warframe can land better than classic fantasy currently does.

Shintar tries WoW Forever on US servers and finds rough sharding, ugly chat, and firsthand proof that the roach army reputation exists for a reason.

Wilhelm rounds up EVE Online’s CSM21 winners and notes how CCP’s extra picks can balance missing viewpoints—or conveniently reinforce its own.

Kelly cheers Democratic gains in the U.S. midterms, highlighting House and Senate wins plus standout races in Texas, Michigan, and Ohio.

Ramen Junkie’s weekly wrap-up is mostly TV talk, with NCIS New York disappointing, NCIS Origins delivering, and a side note about getting back into writing.

Warner sees the U.S. midterms as a welcome win, but argues Stephen Miller’s return means the real fight is only getting started.

Ghastly walks through starting a biological autumn garden, from clearing beds and mulching to companion planting carrots, garlic, lettuce, and more.

Tobold shares that he’s heading into surgery for an enlarged prostate and expects a hospital stay plus a couple weeks away from blogging.

Anarchae breaks down the real cost of being online in Canada, from discounted internet and phone plans to a laptop and NAS.

Roger sets firm boundaries for Questa, his LOTRO quest-narration tool, covering OCR fixes now and future Character and Performance voice modes.

Dave Winer celebrates BonBonWeb’s rollout, pitching Markdown plus RSS as a writer-friendly, silo-resistant way to rebuild a more open web.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 7 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae pokes through Driftwood in Divinity: Original Sin 2, finding dead fish, racist townsfolk, sneaky quests, and very little actual progress.

Aywren is thrilled that Guild Wars 1 is getting new DLC, with Afterlife bringing a dynamic dungeon, skill drafting, and more reasons to revisit Tyria.

Marc looks back at Zack & Wiki on Wii as a motion-control-friendly point-and-click adventure with big cartoon energy and unusually thoughtful design.

Zack says Life is Strange: Double Exposure smartly revisits Max Caulfield and turns the original game’s ending split into a compelling new hook.

Ellie calls The Last of Us Part II exceptional and emotionally crushing, even if its fixation on misery sometimes makes the ride harder than necessary.

Wilhelm hits level 77 in Pokemon Go, with Max Battles the real slog, and already has the XP banked for the push to 78.

Jimmy digs into Deus Ex’s launch reception, long-running mythmaking, and why its reputation needs more historical grounding than internet canon gives it.

The Friendly Necromancer earns EverQuest Legends’ Godslayer title, then wonders whether to keep grinding, jump to Enshrouded, or just heal up first.

Tobold is intrigued by MMO Simulator, a management game about running an MMORPG and watching virtual players react to your design choices.

Cristian posts a brutally short sleep log: just three hours total, split across two rough stretches before dawn.

Scopique rounds up a new Switch 2, early dungeon-crawling fun with Underkeep, and a neat web find in Spelunkr.tv.

Dave Winer unveils BonBonWeb, his Markdown-first “writers web” prototype built around replaceable parts, reader-controlled presentation, and no silos.
